text.en: Asha looked at her father's dimples and her own. "Traits pass from parents to children," said her teacher.

Gregor Johann Mendel is called the Father of Genetics. From his experiments with pea plants he explained inheritance. A monohybrid cross follows one pair of contrasting traits and a dihybrid cross follows two. Mendel's laws include the law of dominance, the law of segregation and the law of independent assortment.
Chromosomes contain DNA and associated proteins. A copied chromosome has two sister chromatids joined at the centromere. They are autosomes and sex chromosomes, and a karyotype is the picture of the chromosome set. DNA has the double helix structure described by Watson and Crick, and it replicates before cell division.
In the usual human chromosome patterns, XX is associated with female development and XY with male development. Other patterns and differences in development also occur. A mutation is a sudden change in the genetic material.
Gregor Johann Mendel is called the Father of Genetics.
From his experiments with pea plants he explained inheritance.
A monohybrid cross follows one pair of contrasting traits and a dihybrid cross follows two.
Mendel's laws include the law of dominance, the law of segregation and the law of independent assortment.
Chromosomes contain DNA and associated proteins. After a chromosome is copied, its two sister chromatids are joined at a region called the centromere.
They are autosomes and sex chromosomes, and a karyotype is the picture of the chromosome set.
DNA has the double helix structure described by Watson and Crick, and it replicates before cell division.
In the usual human chromosome patterns, XX is associated with female development and XY with male development. Other chromosome patterns and differences in development also occur.
Heredity is the passing of biological information between generations. Relatives can share features even though they are not identical.
Mendel studied pea traits such as round and wrinkled seeds. Simple contrasts helped him count recurring patterns across generations.
A gene is a stretch of DNA with a function. Alleles are different versions of the same gene.

board.text: Genes and alleles are different terms

text.en: In a simple model, a pea plant has two alleles for the trait. One inherited allele comes from each parent.

board.text: One allele can come from each parent

text.en: T T and T t are different genotypes. Under complete dominance they can both produce the tall phenotype.
Tall and short are phenotypes in the pea model. Some traits also depend on the environment or on many genes.
T T and t t are homozygous. T t is heterozygous because the two alleles differ.
Dominance describes what happens when two different alleles occur together in this model. A dominant allele need not be the more frequent one.
When gametes form, each gets one allele of the pair. A T t parent can supply either capital T or lowercase t.
In the simple cross T T with t t, each offspring receives one capital T and one lowercase t. The offspring are tall under complete dominance.

board.text: The first generation can look alike

text.en: In T t crossed with T t, list the two possible alleles from each parent. The four equally likely pairings are T T, T t, T t and t t.

board.text: Use the grid for expected outcomes

text.en: A quarter of the model outcomes are T T, half are T t, and a quarter are t t. This gives an expected genotype ratio of one to two to one.

board.text: Genotype probabilities are one, two, one

text.en: T T and T t are both tall under the model. Three of four possibilities are tall and one is short.

board.text: Phenotypes group genotypes that look the same

text.en: A three-to-one expectation does not require every set of four offspring to include one short plant. Repeated observations can differ from the predicted proportion.

board.text: A probability is not a family quota

text.en: Follow seed shape and seed colour together. Use the allele combinations for the two genes to describe each gamete.

board.text: A dihybrid cross tracks two traits

text.en: Genes on different chromosome pairs can assort independently. Closely linked genes on the same chromosome often do not.
In a two-trait cross with independent assortment and complete dominance at both genes, the usual predicted phenotype ratio is nine to three to three to one.

board.text: Read nine to three to three to one as probabilities

text.en: DNA is packaged with proteins in chromosomes. Genes occupy regions along the DNA.
A copied chromosome has two sister chromatids. They are separated when cells divide so new cells can receive a copy.
A karyotype displays chromosomes by features such as size and shape. It gives an overview of a chromosome set.

board.text: A karyotype arranges chromosomes for comparison

text.en: The two strands of DNA pair in a pattern. A pairs with T, and C pairs with G. Complementarity helps explain how cells copy DNA.
A mutation is a change in genetic material. Many have little effect, while some can change traits. Inherited changes can contribute to variation.

problem.en: What tall-to-short ratio is expected across many offspring from a Tt × Tt pea cross, assuming T is completely dominant?

text.en: Tall is dominant.
The offspring are TT, Tt, Tt and tt.
So tall : short is 3 : 1.

problem.en: What is the difference between genotype and phenotype in a Tt pea plant?

text.en: Tt is the genotype.

why.en: It states the allele combination under discussion.

text.en: Tall is the phenotype in this complete-dominance model.

problem.en: In Tt × Tt, what is the chance of one offspring being short?

text.en: List TT, Tt, Tt and tt.

why.en: These are the four equally likely pairings in the simple model.

text.en: Only tt is short, so the chance is one quarter.

why.en: A single offspring does not determine the outcome for the next one.

problem.en: In a simple two-trait model, each gene has a three-quarter chance of showing the dominant trait. What is the chance of both dominant traits if the outcomes are independent?

text.en: Multiply 3/4 by 3/4.
The probability is 9/16.

why.en: It is the expected proportion across many outcomes.

prompt.en: A friend says Mendel worked on fruit flies. How will you reply?

requiredIdeas.en: Fruit flies were used later by Morgan.

points.en: Mendel is the Father of Genetics.
A Tt × Tt cross with complete dominance predicts a 3:1 phenotypic ratio over many offspring.
XX and XY are the usual human sex chromosome patterns.
